reviews.title: The BEST all inclusive tour
reviews.text:
Whole experience was amazing. Was able to book last minute the day before.
It is worth every penny and more affordable than me booking a private car plus admission fees, to take me to Cape Coast. Received pick up location the night before. The driver was friendly. The journey was around 4 hours from Accra but the car was very comfortable with aircon.

Cape Coast castle was quite emotional for me. Wish I had more time as the tour was only 45mins but Elina Castle tour was slightly longer with more time to explore the castle and pay my respects to my ancestors. The tour guides were very knowledgeable.

Pre-ordered lunch before arriving at Kakum National Park which was ready when we arrived. Lots of walking and step steps but that made the experience more enjoyable. The canopy walk was breathtaking, though I didn't look down.

reviews.title: Amazing Experience — Wisdom Was Exceptional!
reviews.text:
I had an amazing experience on this tour from start to finish! Our tour guide, Wisdom, was absolutely wonderful. He was professional, knowledgeable, patient, and extremely attentive throughout the entire day.

What stood out to me most was how genuinely helpful he was. At Kakum National Park, he made sure I was comfortable and assisted me when I needed help, which I truly appreciated. He consistently checked on us throughout the tour and made sure we were enjoying the experience.

We visited Cape Coast, Elmina, and Kakum National Park, so it was a very full and long day, but Wisdom remained attentive and accommodating the entire time. He also went above and beyond to help me with currency exchange when I needed additional cedis, which was not something he had to do but was greatly appreciated.

Wisdom helped make an already memorable experience in Ghana even better. If you’re considering this tour, I highly recommend it—and if you have the opportunity to have Wisdom as your guide, you’ll be in great hands!

100/10 experience!

reviews.title: Impactful Experience. Highly recommend!
reviews.text:
Great day trip. Very impactful stop offs at Cape Coast and Elmina Castles. The canopy walk at Kakum was also fantastic. The lunch option was also great. Would definitely recommend to anybody returning to Ghana with family or ancestral roots and visitors from across the world to see a true, and at times shocking, history of what has impacted us all. The tour guide at both castles were very knowledgable.

The transportation was also very comfortable, with WiFi included. There is ample opportunity to stop along the route at restrooms, ATMs and snack stops.

One thing to be aware of is the current major reconstruction project on the N1 freeway, which is a sizeable part of the journey. It causes a bumpy ride on the way to Cape Coast and traffic delays on return to Accra. It’s no fault of the tour operator (who are great), just poor planning on the part of the freeway contractor!

The tour driver' experience in providing some very interesting history bits during the course of journey was well appreciated. All the three journey locations were nothing short of a rich history experience for my wife and I.

The tour driver did his best to navigate as quickly and as safe as possible to and fro locations but of course, roads under construction and traffic add a considerable amount of time to our journey which is out of the hands of the tour.

Though we arrived home the same day, we did arrive later than expected so it is good to know that external factors can easily add another 1hr or more to the journey but our wonderful tour driver (and also guide during travel time), Mr. Patrick, navigated the roads and chose routes that were comfortable and best for the experience.

All in all, I will say the tour company care about the whole experience and do everything in the ability to keep you informed before and after the journey through WhatsApp and calls.

5/5 for everything and thank you :)

reviews.title: Powerful experience
reviews.text:
My tour of Cape Coast Castle, Elmina Castle, and the Assin Manso Slave River with Expedition Go Tours and our driver, Emanuel, was an incredibly powerful and unforgettable experience.

Emanuel was professional, knowledgeable, and made the entire journey smooth and enjoyable. While the day was emotionally heavy, it was also deeply meaningful. Walking the same paths that my ancestors walked before being forced into slavery was both eye-opening and heartbreaking. There were moments that brought me to tears as I reflected on the suffering, resilience, and strength of those who came before us.

Visiting the castles and Assin Manso gave me a much deeper understanding of history and a stronger appreciation for my origins and heritage. The experience was moving in a way that is difficult to put into words. I also had the opportunity to connect with others and learn more about the history and culture of Ghana, which made the tour even more impactful.

I highly recommend this tour to anyone, but especially to people of African ancestry. It is an emotional journey, but one that provides invaluable perspective, connection, and understanding. Thank you to Expedition Go Tours and Emanuel for helping create such a meaningful experience.

reviews.title: Fantastic experience - breathtaking and informative
reviews.text:
My wife and I enjoyed the hell out of this experience, which was alternately breathtaking, beautiful, and intense (not physically). The scenery is incredible, and the guide and driver did a wonderful job of narrating about the areas we drove through as well as the sites on the itinerary. The sites dealing with the history of slavery are powerful and I find it hard to believe any visitor - especially Americans like us - could visit without being affected.

Be aware that this is a lot of driving, probably close to 5 hours in the van cumulatively. Small children (there were two in our tour group) may have their patience tested. Honestly this is more of an "adults" thing - kids will like the National Park with the jungle canopy walk, but the historical sites will be hard for really small kids to appreciate I believe. That said, a young boy on the tour of Elmina Castle asked the guide, "Did my ancestors have to stay here" and, well, everyone was pretty choked up at that.

Crowds are present at all of these sites. Nothing unmanageable, nothing overwhelming, but be aware that these are all popular things to see - by locals as wel as tourists like me. Go. Do it.

reviews.text:
Mr. T is a deeply knowledgeable and compassionate guide. The tour of the castles was transformative. Kakum was a beautiful way to decompress and connect with nature after the emotional weight of experiencing the nightmare history of the slave trade.
The van trip to get there on the Accra-Cape Coast Road, however was terrible. The 4-star rating is not for this tour company, but for the mismanagement of the road project, which has ruined the livelihoods of the people living along it and was one of the worst travel experiences ever. Tour companies have no choice but to use the road to get from Accra to Cape Coast. Tourists should refuse to travel on this road until it is fixed.

reviews.text:
Great tour of 3 worthy spots in Cape Coast. Michael was an OUTSTANDING tour guide! Very friendly and personable, and really made it pleasant. You get about 2 hours at Kakum, which is about the right amount of time you need, and about 1 hour at each of the castles, which again is about right. Plus the spot for lunch (not included in cost) was excellent.

A bit of emotional whiplash from going from the fun and beauty of the canopy tour… to the cruelty and tragedy on display in the slave castles. But all 3 sites are very worthwhile. Really glad we decided NOT just to stay in Accra during our time to the south.

Make sure you are ok with LONG car trips under arduous conditions on extremely bad roads. We were in the car for about 10 hours total. If I had to do it over again, I might consider an overnight in the Cape Coast area rather than doing it as a day trip from Accra. It was a very long, challenging day.

reviews.title: A great day trip from Accra well worth the long drive
reviews.text:
This was an excellent day trip that was worth the very long drive (almost 3h there and 3h back). The lovely Mr Emmanuel Frempong was my guide. He was very attentive and knowledgeable about the local area and really happy to share everything he knew. I really enjoyed the day and was incredibly moved by the experiences at both Cape coast and Elmina castles. The guided tours at the castles are a well oiled machine and the guides are knowledgeable and efficient. It is worth asking to slow down those parts to allow the guides to give the content the gravity it deserves. Also - if you are a woman alone as I was, it is worth asking Emmanuel to linger a bit with you during the guided tour at the Castle. I was caught off guard by the guide asking me if I was married and asking probing questions right after taking me round one of the slave dungeons. This left me a bit uncomfortable and slightly tainted that experience.

The Kakum national park was a beautiful experience of walking at canopy level in a rainforest. Some brief information about the trees and plants would have been good, but you are at the behest of the guides at the park, where we waited 30mins for our slot to begin, then went off separately with Emmanuel to try and make up the lost time so I didn’t really learn anything about the rainforest and vegetation in Ghana.

Overall I’m so glad I went on this trip, I thought Emmanuel was great company and he couldn’t have done any more to make this trip better. It is a difficult task to achieve all 3 sites in one day starting and returning to Accra with the terrible roads. The experience was worth it all!

reviews.title: A great day out visiting four attractions but a very emotional one.
reviews.text:
I really enjoyed the trip with my partner however it was a very long day but we visited four attractions sites which were Cape Coast castle, Elmina Castle, Kakum national park, Assin Manso Slave River. Our guide Moses was very good and patiently drove us to the attractions and back safely and made it fun for all of us. He took pictures of the day and sent then to us .It was an emotionally charged trip, learning about the slave trade and treatment of slaves in both castles and we did the river walk of our slave ancestors. The tour guides at every attraction was excellent.The Kakum park canopy walk was a great experience but if you are scared of heights then I wouldn't recommend and walking over the rope bridge is daunting.Just a word of warning,the trip is a long about 4 hours each way and also uncomfortable due to ongoing roadworks on the main highways. The roads are very bumpy , not ideal if you travel from car sickness. Make sure you wear comfortable clothing and footwear. Also be mindful that you will be harassed at the sites by people trying to sell you things, they will ask you your name and then they will make you something with your name on it and then want you to buy it, don't fall in that trap, My only criticism of the tours provider is that you were supposed to get bottled water and snacks provided for free throughout the trip. We was only provided with one warm bottle water and NO snacks considering the length of the day. We also had to pay for our own lunch which was not included in the cost of the trip. There is also a tipping culture which was emphasied by our guide Moses and we felt we had to tip the guides in each of the attractions we entered. This can work out expensive if you are visiting four attractions, However in my opinion, there is no obligation to tip unless you want to, it is entirely your choice but be mindful you have paid a considerable amount for the trip,
Having said this it was worth it, especially visiting the four sites we did and was a great experience that everyone coming should go through. Hopefully by that time, the roads will be better making the travelling more enjoyable.

reviews.title: An amazing experience, simply unforgettable!
reviews.text:
We did a day tour to Cape coast from Accra and the tour from the start to the finish was tailored and ended up being like a private tour, because there were only two of us on the tour. Our tour guide George was very friendly, warm and very helpful. He made the experience of the journey very enjoyable and gave it a very personal touch. It honestly felt like we were on a personal road trip with a friend. George accommodated many of our requests, took the most amazing pictures, he is very good at taking pictures that captures the experience and emotions. George was also very good with the locals and made some good recommendations for things and food to try beyond the tour! The Kakum tropical park was great and the canopy walk will definitely get your adrenaline pumping (if you have a heart condition or have a high blood pressure, I wouldn’t recommend doing this) but to finish it is definitely an experience that will make you feel proud! We also tried some fresh palm wine after completing the canopy walk. The trip to the Elmina Castle and cape coast castle was really emotional!!! I wasn’t prepared for that level of emotion. The day and time of the tour was great because it wasn’t busy at all, so we really could explore at our own pace without being overcrowded.

George also recommended other tours and places to visit in Ghana and gave us an authentic history of Ghana that didn’t feel rehearsed or automated. We talked about the geopolitics of the region, the diversity of the people and historical significance of their culture.

After the cape coast tour, we also did the Accra city tour (on a different day) with George and his colleague Joseph. Again this was another excellent tour of really exploring the city. We went to Dr Du Bois museum which was a burst of the pride Pan-Africanism, we visited the national museum filled with rich Ghanaian history that pre-dates the trans-Atlantic slave trade. We also went to Kwame Nkrumah national park and honestly saw the best of Accra even took a trip to the local makola market.

All in all I found the Travio Ghana tour guides (George & Joseph) very professional, friendly, helpful and honest and it seems that they truly enjoy what they do.

I would definitely recommend using this company and definitely a good value for your money.

Began with an early morning pick up and a long drive to Cape Coast. Nothing we can do about that. Stopped and had breakfast about ninety minutes out of Accra. Great little sport in Amun something or other. After breakfast made our way to Kakum National Park for the first adventure. Got to hike and climb and experience the canopy walkways. Fun. Learned about the various trees in the park. Really enjoyed the experience. Had lunch on the ocean. Loved that. After went to the two castles still in existence that were heavily involved in the slave trafficking from Portugal, Denmark, and Britain. The experience is life changing. What you see in books or movies does not do justice to the stark and cold reality of the inhumanity of the men charged with gathering and shipping slaves off to the Caribbean and the United States. Until you see the cramped cells and walk on the hard floors that were covered in the feces and excrement of the men and women who were sold into slavery you have no reference point. It was visceral and gut wrenching. Such a ghoulish and heart rending thing but so thankful to have been able to see it for my own eyes. Thank you Travio Ghana-Tours for a wonderful and touching adventure.

reviews.title: For Those Who Chose the Sea 1619-Present
reviews.text:
There are journeys—and then there are soul pilgrimages. This was the latter.

What was meant to be a celebration with my mother—her third time to Ghana, my first—became a sacred homecoming in her honor. She passed unexpectedly last August, but before her transition, she asked me to bring her home. And with the care, wisdom, and profound presence of Thompson, I did just that.

Thompson was more than a guide. He was a brother, a healer, a historian, and a silent strength who knew how to hold space without words. His knowledge of the land is deep, his spirit is steady, and his compassion made it possible for me to return my mother’s ashes to the sea and sand—not as a moment of loss, but as a powerful act of reclamation.

Cape Coast Day trip with Mosses was a major success. From his timeless, hospitality, to his informative guidance throughout the trip was paramount of what is expected of a Tour guide.

Mosses was on time and detailed on how the day would go. Tour starts at Kukum National Park where you hike through the park. Be prepared and bring sneakers with traction or hiking books, its quick but taxing short hike. Didn’t see any animals so that was kind of a bummer but it was a nice way to work up a sweat to start the day.

The St George Castle at Elmira is the second stop of the trip but first for an emotional journey through the history of the slave trade .

Mosses stops by The Breeze, a pub, bar, and grill by the Beach, not too far from Elmira. Mosses places the order prior to arrival so soon as you get there your food is basically waiting for you. I treated myself to tasty Jollof Rice, with a Steamed Snapper(fresh from the sea of course). It was too good. Feel free to wash it down with a bottle of “Club.”

The trip continues to the pinnacle moment of the day, the Cape Coast castle with the infamous “Door of no Return.” Challenging walk through with the education and history behind the castle as you recognize the tragedy and horrors that took place there. Truly humbling, endearing, and enlightening experience.

Be prepared emotionally and physically for the Cape Coast day tour, but Mosses will make sure you suited to handle the tour to the best of his abilities.

It is worth it!

reviews.title: Must see when in Ghana
reviews.text:
This is a suuuuuper long day. Our guide, Thompson was the complete professional. Knowledgeable, approachable, dynamic and informative. It was a nice small group of 11 which was good. The tree top walk is a great thing to do, but organisation when you get there is extremely poor and the queue is much longer than the walk itself.

The trip to Elmina castle was incredibly informative and well worth the visit. You are absolutely hounded by vendors when you arrive, but Thompson warned us about this and was able to help us manage it.

Cape Coast castle is a must see. Our guide for the castle, Nana Ekow was incredible! The whole trip was harrowing, but history that must be heard and seen.

Overall, it was a great day. I did really struggle to understand why it cost as much as it did, especially when lunch is another 200-250 cedis on top - but I would recommend it as a day to really help you see and understand more of Ghana's history.

After a short coffee break the first stop is Kakum National park with walks on rope bridges and then a short drive to 2 UNESCO castles that were involved in the slave trade. The tour of the castles can be quite harrowing when you learn of the suffering and pain the slaves went through.

reviews.title: Emotional Trip To Elmina & Cape Coast Castle
reviews.text:
It was an early 6:30 am start to beat the rush hour traffic with our guide Joe who was very accommodating and kept us very informed about the trip and contemporary Ghanaian life throughout. This is a full day trip, and we didn't get back until dark as on the way back we hit the Accra rush hour which is not for the faint hearted.

It takes almost three hours (including a 20-minute pit-stop) to get to Kakum National Park. The canopy walk is up to 140 feet in the trees across all manner of narrow bridges and walkways. We walked across all seven bridges in what was an extremely pleasant and adventurous expedition that both children and adults would love, even if you don't have a head for heights.

Then it was on to Elmina and Cape Coast castle. Slave castles.
This part made the excursion an emotional rollercoaster of a day. Historically, the castles complete the links between the plantations of the Caribbean, Americas, and the lands of the African continent.

We called at both Elmina and Cape Coast Castle with a delicious chicken, jollof rice and plantains beach-side lunch in between.

The stories from the castles themselves were quite traumatic and just seeing the whitewashed walls and brilliance of their construction was quite soul destroying. We were witnessing first-hand the well-preserved remnants of what must have been a colossal investment in inhumanity and brutality executed to first class engineering standards. Plus, hearing that a church was built over a dungeon to drown out the cries of the enslaved was very painful to even contemplate that the architects and designers literally thought this all through.

It's always best to remember as well that not all members of the groups listening to the tour guides have an emotional investment in visiting the castles and as a consequence are occasionally apt to say insensitive things out of embarrassment, ignorance or plain stupidity. So best to buckle up emotionally.

Definitely the 'best' excursion of the week, if 'best' is the right word.

reviews.title: Great Sites, Mediocre Tour Company
reviews.text:
The actual sites and stops were nothing short of amazing. Highly recommend visiting all the spots included in the tour. However, those are not because of the tour group directly.
My first issue was pick up time. There was no proper communication of when pick up would be. The night before I was told it would be 6 am. When I asked them to confirm, I heard nothing. At 6 am I was ready and nothing. At 6:05 I called and asked and they told me a driver was on the way. By 6:45, still nothing. Finally around 7, they came. I ended being the only person for the whole tour so I don't know why they were late.
The coordinator I spoke to over the phone agreed to pay for my lunch as a kind gesture, which I appreciated it. In the end that did not even happen and I paid for my own lunch.
Second, the driver I had, Joseph, seemed to be extremely overworked. He explained he had driven to Cape Coast and back the day prior, was doing it the day of my tour, and would be doing it again the next day. I recognize the drive is a lot and quite tiring. He complained constantly throughout the day of how tired he was, and understandably so. I still got to experience all of the sites and had a great time but the overall energy was not exactly enthusiastic.
Lastly, the pdf is inaccurate. They mention a 4:30-5:30 am pickup time for Saturdays (my tour was on a Saturday) and a 7-8 pm drop off. I was picked up at 7 am and dropped off at 9 pm. I did not have a problem with the duration of the tour but rather the inaccuracy of the timing.
I think Travio Ghana could improve on their communication and organization, especially for the price they charge. Overall, I do not think the price they charge is worth the experience through them. It would be cheaper and perhaps more worthwhile to drive yourself or hire a driver since all the stops (the castles, hans cottage, and Kakum) have guides included.

reviews.title: Good, but not a GREAT tour.
reviews.text:
Overall, the Cape Coast tour was a good trip, not a great trip.
Some of the positives from the trip were despite the heavy rain and an unfortunate incident at the beginning of our trip, ever stop was rain free. The guides at each stop were outstanding provided a lot of detailed information about each location and took time to answer any questions from the groups.
The first two stops were fun (canopy and crocodile/bird park) and the two Cape Coast castles were definitely emotional, informative, and eye opening tours.
Our guide to each location was also very nice and gave us some very detailed information about each region and city that we passed on the way to each location.
As for negatives, each location felt rushed...and I can only assume due to a very long delay we had during our trip. I would have liked to have spent more time at the castles, but we were hurried back to our transportation to the next stop as some as the official tour was completed.
The biggest negative was the breakfast and lunch. Although the breakfast was included with the tour, I would have rather brought my own. We received a small meat filled pastrie and very small coffee, which was not filling. I would much prefer paying for the breakfast I wanted and having the cost deducted from the total price.
The lunch was much too late. I would have liked if we would have went after the crocodile/bird park rather than waiting until we finished at the first Cap Coast castle (which was very late in the afternoon, and we were starving).
The lunch was not great at all. Although we pre-ordered before our first castle stop, we still waited almost 30 - 40 minutes after we arrived at the restaurant to be served. It was the most expensive meal I had during my stay in Ghana (average $12 - $14 each) and wasn't much. I had the baked chicken with rice, a few side veggies. and a drink. This meal normally cost about $4 - $5. charging us two to three time of the normal cost is just wrong. If I'm going to spend this much, I would like to get my money's worth. I hope future visitors get their money's worth on future trips and make the lunch stop earlier.
Despite the negatives, I would definitely recommend this trip. With just a few minor changes, it can go from a good trip to an outstanding trip.

reviews.title: Great experience, but a very very very long day
reviews.text:
This tour was supposed to run 6AM - 7PM. In reality, I was picked up at 06:20am, and did not get back to my hotel until 09:30pm. Its a ridiculously long day, and is exhausting sitting in a van for over 7 hours (round trip).

That said, its a good tour overall. My guide for the day was George. I never caught the name of the driver, but he drove like a lunatic (more on this later).

It took over 3 hours to get from Accra to Cape Coast. Over an hour is just getting out of Accra. The driver was honestly awful. He nearly hit other vehicles multiple times, and then literally hit someone on a bicycle about half way to Cape Coast, then claimed it was the biker's fault. The driver was often driving too fast, over taking vehicles unsafely, and weaving around other vehicles. Its a minor miracle that there weren't more accidents.

The actual tour included Kakum National Park (with the canopy walk), Botel Cottage (a tourist trap to pet an alligator), Elmina Castle and Cape Coast Castle. The national park was quite nice, with a truly unique experience. The Botel Cottage was a huge waste of time, and not worth it. The two castles were haunting, intense experiences which document the evil that was the slave trade over the centuries.

George did a decent job setting context around each of the stops, but that was really his only job. There was a local guide at each stop. We also stopped for a (very) late lunch in Cape Coast at nearly 4pm (hitting the biker added over an hour to the day).

Was it a worthwhile experience, sure. But you really need to be prepared for an excessively long, tiring day where half the time is spent driving.

reviews.title: Great day spent seeing Cape Coast with Travio Ghana
reviews.text:
I had a great day trip to Cape Coast with Expedition-go Tours. I traveled alone as a young, foreign woman and felt completely comfortable throughout the trip.

I learned so much about Ghana from Joe, my driver for the day. We chatted a lot about daily life and Ghanaian history, he patiently answered all of my questions while pointing out local landmarks and foods being sold at the street markets.

While the canopy walkway at Kakum National Park and the visit to see the crocodiles at Hans Cottage were super fun activities, the highlight for me was seeing the Elmira and Cape Coast Castles, walking through the castle spaces with excellent guides/historians at each place, while learning more about the important role they played in the events and story of the African slave trade. Very important sites for every American visiting Ghana to see.

Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a hat for the castle tours, bug spray and comfortable tennis shoes for the canopy walk, and Cedis for lunch and any items you might like to purchase from any of the stops (there are some great books sold at the Castles). Prepare for a ~3-3.5 hour drive to Cape Coast from Accra; Travio Ghana provides wifi and great conversation along the way. If you're looking for more adventures around/from Accra, this company offers several other options to check out too!

reviews.title: Great Tour
reviews.text:
Overall, a very enjoyable tour. We booked a group of 4 of us, and we were the only ones on the tour. My only complaint was we were told 6am for pickup, and at 610am we were told pickup wouldn't be until 730am. I wish we had known this earlier and we could have slept in earlier. Because of the later departure time, the traffic was terrible, and we didn't get to Kakum National Park until noon. We did stop at a small gas station for a bathroom break, and our guide bought us a bottle of water, some juice, and a small empanada-like snack.

Once arriving at Kakum, we had to wait around for about 20 minutes for our tour to start. The hike up to the canopy walk is slippery, all uphill/steps, and it was extremely humid. Make sure you bring plenty of water, and maybe a towel or something to wipe the sweat off. We didn't see any wildlife, but walking on the ropes up in the canopy was still fun,

After leaving Kakum, we went to Hans Botel to see the crocodiles. If you are brave enough, you can pet one of them. After that, we went to Elmina Castle. Be prepared for some very aggressive sellers trying to sell you stuff at the Castle entrance (hint- don't tell them your name, or they will have written it on stuff they're selling to try to guilt you in to buying stuff). Elmina was fairly quick, and we made a lunch stop at Da Breeze Restaurant. It was a beautiful spot right on the ocean and a nice rest.

The final stop was Cape Coast Castle. The brutality that took place at both of these castles will just rip your heart out. After that we had another long ride back to the hotel, and got back around 930pm.

My recommendations would be to make sure you bring plenty of water, and maybe some extra snacks. Although they say they include snacks/water, it's only that initial stop at a gas station. Lunch was late and not until about 330pm. Bring good shoes (you don't want to do Kakum in sandals). You're going to spend quite a lot of time in a car/van and will have limited access to bathrooms for most of the day.

Overall, I think it was a great tour and a good way to see a decent cross-section of Ghana.

One of the most amazing tours I have experienced because I was given an excellent history of each location we visited. We interacted with George, our main tour guide and he was excellent at putting Ghana in perspective for us as African American visitors. He pointed out the opportunities and gave us a clear education about the bartering process.

Especially on one on one day tours he was very efficient with time management and inquiring about how to tailor the tours to meet our interest. I will definitely choose George as my tour guide when I return to Ghana.

I look forward to thinking through the next tours that I will take with him. I plan to explore my interest Ghana's fashion, photography and art, and culinary scene.

reviews.title: Excellent last minute trip - highly recommend!
reviews.text:
**Excellent last-minute trip — highly recommended!**

I originally booked a different tour to the Shia Reserve, which had to be cancelled at short notice due to a family emergency with the guide. The team handled this really well, communicating professionally throughout and quickly offering me this alternative, which turned out to be a fantastic experience.

Our guide Patrick was outstanding — professional, knowledgeable, and a very safe driver. He kept the information flowing throughout the day without it ever feeling like a lecture. The vehicle was comfortable with air conditioning, WiFi, and free water, which made the long drive very pleasant.

The highlight for me was Umbrella Rock — well worth the walk to get there. But honestly, the drive itself is part of the experience; passing through small rural villages gives you a genuine glimpse into everyday Ghanaian life that you simply won’t get staying in Accra.

The whole experience was professionally run from start to finish, with great communication at every stage. I’d have no hesitation booking with this company again and would encourage anyone visiting Ghana to consider this tour.

reviews.title: Amazing tour! Amazing tour guide! Great price!
reviews.text: I wish I had encountered this company prior to setting up reservations with another company at the start of my visit. After a very disturbing interaction with another company, I was hesitant to do any further excursions. However, this company operates as an amazing business, with great customer service, and enthusiastic tour guides. Today I had the opportunity to attend an excursion that included Boti Falls, Aburi Gardens, Umbrella Rock, and the first cocoa farm in Ghana. Peter was the tour guide, and he was extremely enthusiastic, very informative, very intuitive and ensured that the conversation was always flowing. He had an amazing personality and was extremely accommodating for whatever we needed. After everyone was picked up, we got on the road just before 9 AM and got back on the road to get back to Accra just after 6 PM. It’s a great one day trip, but please be prepared to pace yourself and know your endurance and fitness level for the hike to Umbrella, Rock and the staircase leading to Boti Falls - Going down is not the issue it’s coming up that can be very tiring after such a serene and relaxing moment. The Cocoa Farm was a nice short visit with samples of the cocoa fruit and the cocoa pod. Aburi Gardens was at the end as that location is closer to Accra and that is where we had a late lunch/early dinner. Aburi Gardens is picturesque and definitely worth the visit. It’s a great way to end the day as walking around the park is completely flat compared to other parts of the excursion. The tour was smooth, the pick up and drop off was timely, and the price is right! I look forward to my next visit to Ghana and will definitely use Expedition Tours again, as well as recommend them to anyone who is coming to Ghana.

reviews.title: Phenomenal Experience
reviews.text: It was good to get outside of Accra and see the natural beauty of Ghana. Seeing the beautiful mountain side that was lush and green and meandering through the quaint towns along the way you get more of a comprehensive experience of the country. Having a chance for a more intimate explanation of regional and national customs and culture was a major plus. The lunch stop had fantastic food. The falls were gorgeous. The geological formations phenomenal. The botanical gardens and more important the guides there were the icing on the cake. reviews.title: Unfortunately, a very disappointing tour.
reviews.text:
We arranged the Expedition Go Tour to Boti Falls, Aburi Gardens & Cocoa Farm Day Tour. We were very disappointed that the tour did not go as planned and we were unable to complete one major part of the trip, the Aburi Gardens visit, because of problems in planning. We had a nice guide and the two sites we did see, Boti Falls and the Cocoa Farm were very interesting. But Expedition Go Tours could have prevented the problems with improved planning.

In the Trip Advisor listing, the pick up was described as starting between 6 AM and 8 AM, however we were told the night before that pick up was between 8:45 and 9:00 am. It turned out that this was too late to start that day.

There were two major problems. Shortly after we started, our tour guide stopped at a tire shop because he thought some of the tires on the vehicle were not safe. We were there about an hour while some of the tires were replaced. When we arrived at the tire shop, there was no traffic. However, by the time we left the tire shop, the traffic was terrible. Our guide rearranged the order of the trip, which was fine with the group, with the plan to visit Aburi Gardens last.

Once we left the tire shop, the traffic was stop and go for well over an hour. Our guide told us that funerals were often held outside of Accra on the first Saturday of the month, which was the reason for all the traffic. Once we reached our first stop at the Cocoa Farm tour, it after noon. After that we stopped for lunch and drove to Boti Falls. We left Boti Falls just before 5:00 pm and about halfway to the Aburi Gardens, we hit stop and go traffic again, which was now leaving the funeral. It gets dark at 6:00pm and a little before 7:00 our guide asked us if we wanted to go to the Aburi Gardens or skip it and go back to town. Because it was so late and dark we decided to skip the Gardens. (Also, while our guide said they had lights, if you look at the Aburi Gardens website, they close at 4:30.) We got back to our hotel around 8:00 pm without going to the Aburi Gardens. No offer was made of a partial refund for the missed part of the tour.

My family and I believe poor planning on the part of Expedition Go Tours was the cause of the poor trip and we have requested a partial refund (I do not know yet if this has been granted.) First, while we appreciate our guide’s concern for vehicle safety, the company should maintain their vehicles and the tires should have been checked and replaced before the trip, not when we were in the car. This was a huge delay. Second, our guide did not seem surprised by the funerals that day; if certain days are known for funerals, the trips should start earlier on those days to get ahead of the traffic. We ended up being very disappointed in this tour.

reviews.title: Disappointing and grueling day, due partly to negligence of tour company
reviews.text:
Our 11-hours-long tour (ostensibly Boti Falls and Aburi Gardens plus smaller attractions) had several serious problems which seem partially due to negligence by the company.
One set of problems surrounded pickup time. The company posted that pickup would be between 6 and 8 a.m. After I texted the night before, I was told pickup would be by 9; but the car finally came at 9:15. After less than 1 h., the guide stopped to repair several of the tyres, delaying us another hour or so. (Expedition Go Tours should have carefully inspected the vehicle in advance, applying a thorough and rigorous maintenance schedule before driving visitors around Ghana.) We spent hours stuck in traffic due to several funerals along the route (which Expedition Go should have anticipated or researched in advance, for example by picking us up early to avoid congestion).
Finally, although our tour was 11 hours long, we missed completely Aburi Gardens, which was our primary attraction. We have asked the company to refund half our payment for that omission; but they have yet to agree a week later.
Boti Falls was worth seeing; but the trident palm tree was not worth the drive. The cocoa farm was interesting in that we got to sample an actual cacao bean; but commercial cocoa farms nearby in the same region of Ghana are much more impressive, representative, and interesting. The same historical perspective could be provided at them with a better view of how cocoa is actually grown commercially.

reviews.title: Exceeded My Expectations 10/10
reviews.text:
Thank you so much for everything you did to make this journey so special. I have been looking forward to responding because I truly wanted to express how grateful we are.

Our experience with Expedition Go Tours exceeded every expectation. The level of professionalism, organization, and exceptional service your team provided from beginning to end made us feel welcomed, cared for, and safe throughout our journey.

What made this trip extraordinary, however, were the people. Our guides quickly became more than guides—they became family. They didn't simply take us from one destination to another; they walked alongside us, shared their hearts, answered every question with patience, and gave us a genuine understanding of Ghana's history, culture, traditions, and people. Their passion was contagious, and because of them, we experienced Ghana in a way that no guidebook could ever provide.

As a group, my clients and I left Ghana forever changed. We laughed together, reflected together, and experienced emotions that are difficult to put into words. Standing in places like Cape Coast, being welcomed by families during our naming ceremony, sharing meals, and interacting with so many beautiful people created memories that will stay with us for a lifetime. We didn't feel like tourists—we felt connected to the culture, the history, and the people.

Please extend our heartfelt gratitude to everyone who played a part in making this journey so meaningful, especially our guides. Their kindness, professionalism, and genuine care made all the difference, and they represented Expedition Go Tours with excellence.

Thank you again for helping create an experience that touched our hearts and strengthened our connection to Ghana. I look forward to bringing many more groups to experience the same warmth, excellence, and hospitality that Expedition Go Tours provided.

With sincere appreciation,

Julia

reviews.title: Accra Essentials: A Cultural and Historical Introduction
reviews.text:
This was the very first tour we took during our trip to Accra, and I’m glad we started here. It provided an excellent foundation, touching on many of the essentials needed to understand the city’s landmarks and culture. If you want a meaningful introduction to Accra, this tour delivers. Our guide, Matthew, was communicative, courteous, accommodating, and professional—qualities that made the experience even more enjoyable. Pick up and drop off were great! Matthew was punctual, conscious of the timing during the tour, and the transportation was comfortable.

W.E.B. Du Bois Center – A glimpse into the man with the vision. Our tour guide at the Center, Kofi, offered a clear and insightful overview of Du Bois’s life, influence, and legacy. Experiencing this history in the home where Dubois lived as a Ghanaian citizen in his final years—and where his body now rests—was moving.

Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park – A beautiful and meaningful tribute to the man who led Ghana to independence. The grounds themselves are striking, especially the fountain and the mausoleum. The tour highlighted both the triumphs and the struggles of the independence movement, the diplomatic efforts that shaped it, and the enduring legacy of Nkrumah’s leadership. Standing here, you feel the weight of history and the pride of a nation.

Independence Square – A landmark of national significance, used for government ceremonies and large public events, but also available for private gatherings. The Freedom & Justice monument commemorating Ghana's independence stands majestically on one side of the street, and across the street, the Black Star Arch looks proudly over the square with the ocean in the background. Independence Square is a simple yet powerful symbol of Ghana’s identity.

National Museum of Ghana – A quick yet fascinating anthropological journey through Ghana’s past. The exhibits begin with early artifacts and tools excavated from the region, then expand into the diverse cultures that make up modern Ghana. The museum offers a vivid window into traditions, customs, and colorful celebrations that define the nation’s heritage.

Makola Market – What a spectacle! No description could prepare me for the sheer size and scope of this market. Our guide, Matthew, led us up five flights of stairs to the top of a parking structure for a bird’s-eye view—and only then did I understand the scale. To walk every street, corridor, and booth would take miles and more than a day. Vendors stretch as far as the eye can see.

Important Note: This tour is not designed for shopping at Makola Market. If you want to spend time browsing and buying, I recommend visiting on your own or joining a tour dedicated solely to the market. Here, the purpose is to grasp the awe of its scale. Thankfully, Matthew later took us to a smaller market where we could buy souvenirs. That thoughtful adjustment made the experience smoother, as coordinating shopping for a group—even our small group of five—would have consumed the rest of the day.

reviews.title: Great Driver, average tour
reviews.text:
First thing to say is that our driver and lead tour guide Thompson aka Mr T was fantastic, he was engaging, knowledgeable and flexible given we went on this tour with our 4 month old baby. The best bits of the tour were the bits that he led

The downfall, however, was that he didn't lead the whole thing. When we went to different monuments, we had guides from those places take us around and the quality varied wildly, e.g we had a guide at the WEB Dubois museum who in the room dedicated to pan africanist leaders, could not explain what pan Africanism was. This tour structure led to going to lots of monuments and just having things pointed out to you, this is x, this is y without at any point a clear and overarching narrative of the history or story of Ghana ever being explained. This wasn't aided by the constant handing over from person to person as it meant often things were repeated as they did not know what the previous person had said, and no wholisitc narrative was built. The best portion of the tour was the Dr Kwame Nkrumah memorial Park which Mr T led.

The tour could have been great if we had one person with us the whole time taking us through the all the stops, who could tell a story of the history of Ghana that runs through the monuments and leaves you with a clearer impression of the country. With that in mind, the order should be different too, we should start at the museum of Ghana, then W e B Dubois house, then independence square/gate then the markets and then finish at Dr Kwame Nkrumah memorial park.

reviews.title: Did I experience everything I paid for? NO.  Was I offered compensation or a plan B? NO
reviews.text:
The Accra City Tour - I had a great experience on this trip, until the rain started.
Our driver and guide Emmanuel was attentive to our needs, informative about the local sites we saw and very calm & reassuring during challenging situations.

This trip is NOT 5 stars because;
Did I see everything that i paid for on this trip? NO
Did I experience each place in equal measure ie 60 mins? NO
Was I offered compensation or an alternative plan because the rain prevented us from fulfilling our programme? NO

At the W. E.B Debois centre we had ample time to see the place, be guided by the guide at the centre and visit the shop on site

At the National Museum of Ghana it was a good experience and we had plenty of time to listen to the guide ask questions and see the place

We had a very nice lunch break just off Oxford street, that was a pleasant experience and a very nice place, the food was beautiful.

During lunch the rain started.

Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park, we drove through heavy rain to the park. Inside at reception we sheltered for more than 1 hour waiting for the rain to stop, before the guide at the centre took us out. In the rain we were guided through the park to the different areas, it was informative but NOT ENJOYABLE. By the end of the tour it is still raining heavily 2 members of our group did not have an umbrella as I did so they were not interested in continuing this tour in the rain.

As it was obvious the rain was not going to stop any time soon I consulted our guide Emmanuel about the possibility of compensation or to continue this program another day as I would be available next week to do so. His response from his managers was that non of these options would be possible.

I am not pleased with this response because I have paid in good faith expecting Expedition Go to honor the program I have paid for or have a plan B. I would not recommend this company because of this lack of provision in situations like this. I’m sure this is not the first time this has happened. Yes sometimes it rains, but if Expedition Go are not able to fulfill their part of the deal, as customers we should be offered something.

Makola market - Saw it from the car as we past it, through heavy rain.
Was I able to stop and see the place? NO
Was I able to explore it? NO
I didn’t leave the car and no plan B was offered to return another day or be compensated because of the rain
As a result I was not able to purchase any gifts which I had hoped I could do on this trip

Independence Square Parade ground - Did I spend quality time here? NO
no plan B was offered to compensate

I saw the parade ground from the car mainly. Stood in the parade ground for less than 5 mins in the rain with my umbrella.
Did I enjoy the experience? NO
Did I get to explore and see this place properly? NO

Black Star Square- Did i spend quality time here? NO
no plan B was offered to compensate.
rain stopped us from going across the busy road, so I have no photos of Black Star Square

Centre for National Culture - I DID NOT VISIT THIS PLACE on our programme & no plan B was offered to compensate for this.

I am still very dissatisfied and disappointed that I don’t have a full experience of the places I have paid to see and the inconvenience of not being able to shop in the market, is a very big disappointment.
This experience means I will not book a visit to cape coast castle with Expedition Go, as I had planned to, unless Management at Expedition Go are willing to remedy this.Did I

reviews.title: Excellent tour of Cape Coast,  Slave Dungeons & Kakum Park, Boti Falls, Day tour Accra
reviews.text:
Cape Coast Trip was a truly humbling experience for me , knowing that an accident of fate had ensured I was not born in Ghana & West Africa during the slave trade. The speakers in Cape Castle & Almina castles( euphemism for dungeons) were passionate & committed guides to the history of those years.
Ebenezer was our tour guide & he kept us all well engaged with his information, his humour & his ability to help us with the local food & customs.
The Canopy bridge of Kakum Park was definitely a high point of the tour .
The 2nd day we went to Boti Falls which was a surreal experience as though we discovered it ourselves as the pristine quality of the surroundings .We requested Ebenezer to be our tour guide as we had completely settled down with his easy & informative ways .
The 3 rd day , today was the Accra trip , starting with an inspirational journey with Du Bois Museum , continuing with Kwame Nkrumah National Park, ending at the Independence Square, finally immersing ourselves in the crowds of Makola Market & under the guiding hands of Ebenezer eating a hearty lunch.
All 3 days helped me to know about Ghanaian culture & feel part of it. Ebenezer as a tour guide was really good & I highly recommend him.

reviews.title: Take lots of pictures. This is epic.
reviews.text:
What a wonderful Wednesday trip. Picked up promptly and got the tour underway with introductions of the tour guide and other passengers. Drove through Accra and talked about the city and driving around the city. First stop was at the W.E.B. DuBois Center. Truly a treat. Got to walk through one of the great minds home and now Museum and see his handwritten notes, his library, and mausoleum and resting place. Incredible. Thank you Victoria for your knowledge and dedication.
From there we made our way to the Center for National Culture. Another Museum. Great experience. The docent was passionate about the Ghanaian culture and history. Very grateful to have Mystic Mike guide us. Very insightful.
After the museum we went to Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park. A must see experience. Absolutely beautiful and stunning. Nkrumah is an amazing person and Ghana leader. Have to see the memorial and appreciate the sacrifices Nkrumah suffered for his country. Just a ten minute walk from the park went to the hustling Makola Market. If you come to Accra you have to go to Makola Market. It’s high-level crazy bargaining and bargains if you know what you want. Definitely, not a place for the timid.
Last place on the tour was Independence Square. I knew it as Black Star Gate. Another iconic Instagram photo opportunity. Absolutely loved the tour. Completely worth every penny. Highly recommend.

reviews.title: Best last day in Ghana
reviews.text:
My friend and I decided only the day before to do this tour.

Our tour guide Eben picked us up at the hotel. It is our last day in Ghana as we are going home tomorrow.

We had already visited Kwame Nkrumah memorial park so we asked Eben to skip that part. It was no problem. Instead we started visiting the W.E.B. DuBois Carter which was very interesting.

Eben had a great knowlegde of everything and he shared it with us.

Next stop was Center for national culture. Then we had lunch (not included). It was a great experience, even if the food was not like we are used to. I am glad we tasted it.

Next stop was Markola market. Eben managed to find everything we needed. But I am so glad we had someone with knowledge of the market with us.

As we skipped the mermorial park, Eben took us to the art center instead.

At last we ended up visiting the independece square.

Eben was by far the best guide we had in this trip to Africa (we also visited Togo). He was fun, knowlegdable and caring. We highly recommend him. He þade our last day here special.

My friend works as a tour guide in Iceland, if Eben ever decides to visit our country, she would guide him.

reviews.title: Best Value! Best Experience!
reviews.text:
I cannot say enough good things about the professionalism, knowledge and ease of booking with this company!!! Our driver Daniel was so laid back and with us every step of the way making sure we were comfortable and safe! He was truly a pleasure and even gave us some history about some of the areas that we passed by on the way to our excursion. If you want quality tours, affordable prices and reliable services please book right now!!!!
Tips for the excursions: pack your favorite light snacks or breakfast bars. We did stop for snacks on each excursion but I found it hard to find breakfast items that were quick and on the go, we traveled from the US. There are NO breakfast sandwiches that I’ve seen in Ghana (bacon, egg and cheese croissants, sausage biscuits, bagels and cream cheese), no prepackaged granola bars, so you’ll want to visit a ShopRite grocery store in the area to buy foods to have for early morning activities or bring them from wherever you’re traveling from.
Water and fun was provided!!! Get your camera and video settings prepared once you book because the memories will be priceless!!

reviews.text:
Ebenezer proved to be an exemplary tour guide, ensuring that my father, cousin, and I had a memorable and enriching experience. Of particular importance was the sense of safety we felt throughout the excursion. While we have participated in similar tours facilitated by other providers whilst here in Ghana, we often experienced a degree of unease with the driving practices of some operators. In contrast, Ebenezer’s professionalism and attentiveness as a driver greatly contributed to our comfort and confidence during the journey.

From a personal standpoint, I was especially appreciative of the manner in which Ebenezer adapted the itinerary to accommodate the needs of the elder member of our group—my father—without diminishing the experience for other participants. His ability to discreetly adjust aspects of the tour, such as moderating the physical demands of certain activities (e.g., climbing), while maintaining the dignity and inclusion of all group members, was commendable. This level of sensitivity exemplifies a high standard of practice in inclusive tourism.

Furthermore, the thoughtful incorporation of smaller, culturally significant stops—such as our visit to Hot Oven to sample freshly baked Ghanaian bread—enhanced the authenticity of the overall experience.
On this basis, I would strongly recommend Ebenezer’s services to prospective visitors.

reviews.text: We had a very enjoyable Accra City Tour with our guide, Thomson, who was friendly, knowledgeable, and passionate about sharing Ghana’s history and culture. We visited important landmarks including Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park, Independence Square (Black Star Square), and the Ghana National Museum, which were all fascinating and well explained. We didn’t get to stop at the W.E.B. Du Bois Center, and although we passed Makola Market, we didn’t go inside. Instead, we spent time at the art market, which was lively and full of unique crafts. The only suggestion for improvement would be a bit more guidance at the market, especially around haggling and typical price ranges, as it can be difficult for visitors to know what’s reasonable to pay. That said, Thomson was professional and helpful throughout, and we appreciated his warm approach and local insights. Overall, it was a great introduction to Accra, and we’re glad we took the tour. Thank you, Thomson!

At Boti Falls you have the choice of taking a hike to Umbrella Rock (approx. 2h total) or drive there after visiting the waterfalls. We chose to do the hike and dont regret it at all. Just make sure to bring water. For lunch, we stopped at a restaurant before visiting the waterfalls to place our orders, so when we came back the meals would be ready. Beacuse we spent alot of time at the falls, we ate at around 5pm. At no point during the Tour are there any hidden fees and we never felt pressured to buy anything. The restaurant has a menu with prices. Van has AC. Emmanuel was always in contact with the staff to ensure we didnt have to wait.

Me, my auntie, mum and cousins speak both English and Twi and our guide (Moses) was so accommodating, kind and made great conversation with all of us in both English and Twi. He was very knowledgeable about the places we were going to. The only gripe I have is the listing does not specify how difficult the hike to the umbrella rock would be as a result my mum and auntie had to cut the hike short and head back to the entrance. However the food we ate in between was amazing the people at each place were so kind. Our transportation was very comfortable which if you know Accra is not usually how the transportation is like so it was a nice surprise. Whenever I come to Ghana I would only book with this company again. Great for people who love nature and history.

reviews.text: The day trip was great and definitely lived up to the description. The rock viewpoint, botanical garden, waterfall etc were worth visiting and I especially enjoyed the cacao farm. Patrick was a great guide, sharing historical knowledge and always ready to answer questions. And there was really good flexibility around logistics of the trip, including requested end-time. Thank you! One thing that made the trip less good and somewhat sad, was the amount of rubbish at all locations. Plastic bottles and cups, candy wrappers etc. were all over the place, including at the waterfall. It was hard to enjoy the beauty of nature with litter everywhere and it partially ruined the trip for me. This is clearly not the responsibility of the tour company, but maybe they could help create financial incentives for local people to do a regular clean-up and educate people about littering. I would happily pay extra for the trip for that money to support local economies, creating jobs and clean nature.
